entries.name: rocks-small
entries.note: MISLABELLED: this frame is a sixth plant, a tall grass tuft, not a rock. The sheet carries six plants and seven rock groups; the tileset was written for five and eight, so every id from this frame on names the picture before it. The id is live in three rockPool entries of urban.mapping.json, which is why it is recorded here rather than quietly corrected: renaming it is a content change with its own review, not a re-export.

note:
Twenty frames in a row: seven repeating ground fields, six plants and seven rock groups, drawn by ImageGen against black at roughly twice the size they ship at. It loads as an auto-strip — the game finds the frames by alpha at load and a tile pins the frame index it resolves to — so order IS the address and moving a piece renames every piece after it. Its alpha was keyed in by art-source/tilesets/key_background.py, per band: the seven fields are keyed solid, because a field is a rectangle where it is drawn and every pixel a key carves off its rim is a puncture the tiling repeats; the plants and rocks are keyed at a much lower threshold, because their own black outlines sit inside the range the fields call background. A rock is several stones, so its band spans the daylight inside it.

Five frames do not take their picture from this plate: grass-1, grass-2, dirt-1, dirt-2 and sand each name a tileable material under atlas-material-source/game-buffs-*, and each is exported at the material's own size plus the renderer's ground inset wrapped round it, so the inset crops back to exactly the material. The ImageGen fields underneath them are still on the plate and are deliberately not what ships: they are slabs with a lit rim and a shadowed skirt, and they repeat visibly. The other two fields, water-1 and water-2, are plate art and keep their authored spriteBorderPx.

The ids below are live: urban.mapping.json names every plant and rock in its NATURE_* pools and TileManifest.pickNatureGrassTileId / pickNatureDirtTileId name the four field variants. The atlas has derived nature-tiles_height.png and _normal.png beside it, sampled at the same pixels; re-run 'gradlew.bat :asset-pipeline:deriveTileMaps' after any export or they read the relief of the sheet they replaced.
